**Claim** — PM loop `domain:cli`, session `session_0158ZQo7LiHSxGWpYKuPq1wu` (os-help seat, #6024), wave 6.

**Unblocked**: held behind #7526, which landed minutes ago as PR #7584 (`cc3555e78`).

⚠️ **And that landing is directly relevant to this card — read it before starting.** #7584 added a **route-ledger ↔ live-mount parity gate** that boots a real server, reads the mount table off it, and asserts every ledgered route is *reachably* mounted — explicitly distinguishing "mounted but shadowed by a catch-all sibling" from "answers". **This card is that exact class**: `POST /api/v1/packages/publish` is ledgered (`rest-route-ledger.ts`, `source: direct-mount`, `disposition: server-only`) and is absorbed by `/packages/:id` with `id = "publish"`, which is where the misleading `Allowed: DELETE, GET, HEAD, PATCH` comes from — that header is **another route's** method set.

**First question for the dev, before any fix**: does the new gate already flag this? If not, **why not** — the plausible answer is that the REST package routes are **service-gated** and never register on a stack without the package service, so a conditional registration may be a shape the gate does not yet model. That answer matters more than the individual route: a parity gate that silently tolerates conditional mounts has the same blind spot the old ledger-as-observation guard had.

- **Branch**: `claude/issue-7563-packages-publish-mount-or-404`
- **The card names the acceptable outcomes** — either the real publish handler answers, or an honest **404** for a surface not mounted on this host. ⛔ What is not acceptable is the status quo: *a 405 whose `Allowed` set describes another route's methods is the one answer that misinforms.*
- **File surface (expected)**: `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts` and/or the registrar wiring, possibly the ledger. ⛔ **Do not touch `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`'s `/meta/app` handler** — #7566 is dispatched to it in the same wave.
- **Prior art**: #3610 / PR #3621 moved publish onto `/packages/publish` in the first place. This is not a regression of that fix — it is the residue it did not cover: what the `/packages` prefix answers on a host where only one of the two owners is mounted. Say which of the two outcomes you chose and why.
- **Tier / container**: M · `claude-opus-5` · `mode:cloud`.

<!-- os-dev-report -->
**os-dev-report** — issue #7563 · branch `claude/issue-7563-packages-publish-mount-or-404` · draft PR #7666 · commit `10f9463`

## Outcome chosen: **both**, and the card's two options turned out to be two different defects

**The real publish handler answers** wherever a `package` service is composed; an **honest 404** naming the surface everywhere else. Not a hedge — investigating the mount produced two independent causes, one per option.

### Cause 1 — the gate was a boot-instant snapshot, and showcase *does* have the service

The card's premise ("no publish surface is served on this host") is true of the wire and **false of the composition**. `examples/app-showcase/objectstack.config.ts:108` declares `requires: [… 'marketplace' …]`, which `serve.ts` resolves to `PackageServicePlugin`. The measurement:

| fact | location |
|---|---|
| `createRestApiPlugin` registered | `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:2138` |
| `PackageServicePlugin` registered (capability-provider loop) | `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:2414` |
| `resolvePluginOrder` preserves insertion order for plugins with no edge | `packages/core/src/plugin-order.ts` |
| `RestApiPlugin` declares only `optionalDependencies: ['com.objectstack.engine.objectql']` | `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts:99` |
| `PackageServicePlugin` registers `package` in `start()`, declares no deps | `packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts:60,197` |

So REST's `start()` asks `getService('package')` **before** the service exists, on precisely the deployments that have one. The service is now handed to the registrar as a **resolver** and read per request — the answer no longer encodes composition order.

### Cause 2 — "not mounted" never degraded to 404 for this path

`POST /packages/publish` has no dispatcher twin (the dispatcher owns `POST /packages` install and `POST /packages/:id/publish`). With nobody owning it, `HonoHttpServer.allowedMethodsForPath()` (`adapter.ts:632`) matched the concrete path against **every** registered pattern **ignoring the request method**, found `/packages/:id` under GET/DELETE/PATCH, and built `405 Allow: DELETE, GET, HEAD, PATCH`. It now mounts unconditionally and answers its own 404 naming the surface.

**404 not 503**: a deployment that composed no marketplace capability will not grow one on retry, and 503 invites exactly that. It is also what `direct-mount-composition.ts` has always documented as the answer for a skipped registrar — until now that promise was simply false on the wire for this one path.

**The other three package routes deliberately do NOT follow.** `GET /packages`, `GET /packages/:id`, `DELETE /packages/:id` each shadow a live dispatcher twin at a byte-identical pattern; mounting them without a service would replace three working routes with a degraded refusal. Pinned so a later "make it consistent" edit goes red.

---

## The parity-gate question you asked first: **no, it did not flag this — and the reason generalises**

`POST /api/v1/packages/publish` was **pinned** in `UNEXERCISED_BY_THIS_BOOT`, reasoned as *"the registrar mounts only when a `package` service occupies the slot; the showcase registers none."* Your hypothesis was right that conditional mounts are the unmodelled shape — but the precise failure is sharper than "the gate can't see it":

> **The reason was true and the conclusion was wrong. An unmounted route is not automatically an *unanswered* one.**

A pin claims "this boot cannot observe it" and was read as "therefore nothing happens here". For this row something very much happened — the exact *"LEDGERED BUT NOT MOUNTED, and DISGUISED"* failure the gate spells out for every **unpinned** row. Conditional mounts were excused from the one check that would have caught them.

**Fixed in the gate, not just for this route.** The pin is deleted (the route is observable for real now) and the pin rule is tightened: *a pinned path that any other pattern matches now fails the gate.*

⚠️ **And there is a trap in that fix worth recording.** The first version probed with `resolveMountedRoute(row.method, path)` and **failed to fail** under mutation. This class is invisible to a method-scoped check: nothing registers `POST` on `/packages/:id`, so the method-aware resolver reports a clean absence, while the 405 seam ignores the request method entirely. The shipped check probes **GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE** and fails if *any* verb matches. Mutation-proved (M7).

### A second measurement — real, unfixed, and NOT this card

The parity gate compares **patterns**, and REST and the dispatcher register byte-identical strings for the three `:id` package routes. So the REST registrar sitting out on a live `objectstack serve` boot (cause 1) is **invisible to the gate**: `rest-route-ledger.ts` says those three "shadow the dispatcher twin (registered first)", and on showcase they currently do not. Behaviour differs — the REST list route merges registry + database packages, the dispatcher's does not. **Left alone deliberately**: changing which owner serves `GET /packages` on showcase is beyond this card's scope and carries its own regression risk. Recommend a follow-up issue.

---

## Changes

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts` | 2nd param → `PackageServiceResolver`; publish route split out and always mounted, resolving the service per request, 404 when absent; the three gated routes take the resolved service, bodies unchanged |
| `packages/rest/src/direct-mount-composition.ts` | registrar called on every boot with the resolver; docs corrected |
| `packages/rest/src/direct-mount.ts`, `rest-route-ledger.ts` | the "not mounted ⇒ not enumerable" rule and the ledger note now say three-of-four |
| `packages/qa/dogfood/test/route-ledger-live-mount-parity.dogfood.test.ts` | pin deleted; all-verbs disguise check added; live-router + live-wire pins for #7563 |
| `packages/rest/src/package-publish-mount.test.ts` | **new**, 10 cases |
| `packages/rest/src/direct-mount-introspection.test.ts` | publish moved to the unconditional cohort; guard that the split row really exists in the ledger |
| `.changeset/packages-publish-mount-or-404.md` | **new** |

⛔ `rest-server.ts` untouched (#7566 owns `/meta/app`). ⛔ no `content/docs/releases/**`.

## Mutation table — every new test proved able to fail

| # | mutation | red |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | publish back to service-gated (`: []`) | 8 cases across both rest files |
| M2 | 404 → 503 / `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | `404s with a message about THIS surface…` |
| M3 | message names a package id, not the surface | `404s with a message about THIS surface…` |
| M4 | mount the gated three unconditionally too | 5 cases incl. `keeps its hands off the three dispatcher twins` |
| M5 | resolve the service eagerly at mount | `runs the real handler when the service arrives AFTER the mount decision` |
| M6 | 404 before the anonymous-deny gate | `refuses an anonymous caller before disclosing whether the surface exists here` |
| M7 | revert the mount **and** re-add the pin (dist rebuilt) | `no pinned path is matched by any OTHER pattern, under any verb` **and** `POST /packages/publish is owned by the publish route…` |

M7 needed a `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest build` between mutation and run — the dogfood harness boots from `dist`, so a source-only mutation is a false green there.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint` ✅ · `pnpm typecheck` ✅ 126/126
- `@objectstack/rest` full suite ✅ **1415 passed / 88 files**
- **the new parity gate** ✅ 8 passed (live showcase boot; `POST /api/v1/packages/publish` → **404**, no `Allow` header, message names the surface)
- `pnpm check:route-envelope` ✅ · `@objectstack/client` ledger-coverage + url-conformance + response-schema ✅

CI not awaited, auto-merge not armed, per dispatch.
